title: Incident
description: The one canonical incident object. Every part of the system reads and writes this shape.

status.description: failed and insufficient_evidence are distinct: could-not-determine is not the same as no-cause-found.

scenario.description: Which fixture produced this incident. Null once providers are real.

alert.description: The alert as it arrived. Closed and required: an empty object used to satisfy this, so an incident could claim a source that said nothing, and a typo'd key rode along unread.

observations.description: Each key is either a collected object or explicitly null. A missing key is a schema error, not an empty observation; an empty object is not a collection; and a collected observation now has to have the shape its provider actually returns, rather than being any object at all.

kubernetes.description: null means nothing was collected. Anything else must match the fixture contract for this slot — see schemas/observations.schema.json, which is derived from the scenario fixtures and is named a contract, not a provider shape, because that is the size of the evidence behind it.

logs.description: null means nothing was collected. Anything else must match the fixture contract for this slot — see schemas/observations.schema.json, which is derived from the scenario fixtures and is named a contract, not a provider shape, because that is the size of the evidence behind it.

root_cause_code.description: A named cause, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, or null when nothing has been concluded yet. The causes come from common.schema.json so that an agent's hypothesis and an incident's verdict cannot drift apart.

supports.description: Which way this points. Required: an unstated direction was indistinguishable from support, so an incident could be diagnosed on evidence that in fact contradicted it.

collection.description: The outcome of collecting each slot, recorded in the document rather than handed back on the side. Codex, 2026-09-05: the failures used to live outside the incident, so once it was serialised the fact that a slot had failed was gone entirely.

kubernetes.description: What happened when this slot was collected. Three answers, not two: an observation, an established absence, and a failure to look. Absence and failure both leave the observation null, and a reader that sees only null cannot tell 'the provider looked and found nothing' from 'nobody looked'.

state.description: collected: an observation is present. nothing: the provider said explicitly that there was nothing here. failed: the slot could not be collected, and the incident is missing it.

kind.description: Only for state failed. absent: nothing was there to read. unreadable: something was there and could not be understood. contradiction: something was there and disagreed with the request it was gathered under.

reason.description: Only for state failed. Why the slot could not be collected, in the words of whatever refused it.

allOf.description: A diagnosed incident must carry a code, a confidence and at least one piece of evidence. Absence is not a diagnosis.

confidence.description: Zero confidence is not a diagnosis. No upper threshold is set here because none has been measured.

evidence.description: At least one piece of evidence must point FOR the conclusion. A diagnosis resting only on contradicting evidence used to pass.

agents.description: At least one agent must have RUN. minItems alone counted an agent whose status is error — which the agent-result schema defines as could not run — so a diagnosis could rest on one failed attempt and nothing else. Found by a subagent on 2026-09-07, measured through the real validator.

allOf.description: insufficient_evidence must say so in the code, so the two states cannot silently merge.

An incident that has not concluded, or that is finished with the book shut, may not carry a live diagnosis. Only diagnosed and insufficient_evidence had conditional rules at all, so status failed with a named cause at confidence 1 and zero agents validated. Written on 2026-09-07 naming failed and closed in its own description — and listing failed and INVESTIGATING in the enum, so closed stayed uncovered. Found the same day by a subagent that ran all four statuses instead of reading the sentence. The description and the rule are two carriers of one claim, and the prose one was right.

root_cause_code.description: An incident that has not concluded has no cause. failed means the chain broke; investigating means it has not finished.
